name: Brian Mast

items.text: Business Insider reported in 2021 that Mast disclosed a July 2021 purchase of up to $100,000 in Virgin Galactic stock on Aug. 23. That may have missed a federal reporting deadline, though the report said the longer 45-day limit would likely protect him. The company's president had testified to a House subcommittee Mast sits on weeks earlier. No finding was reported.
items.why: A late stock-trade disclosure is a smaller filing violation under criterion 6, so it takes the minor weight of 1.
These are Mast's own words about Gaza, a stance on a foreign war that doesn't match any criterion (no conduct on foreign money, self-dealing or doing the job), so it is left off.

items.text: In 2016 a company press release named Mast to the advisory board of World Patent Marketing, which the FTC later sued. Mast said he never received pay and learned of it from a news release. His office said he never served on the board. He returned a donation from the company's owner.
items.why: The reporting shows only that the company's press release named him, with no wrongdoing by Mast shown, so this is guilt by association under criterion 6.

items.text: After Hamas's Oct. 7, 2023 attack on Israel, Mast, an Army veteran, wore an Israeli military uniform in Congress, according to HuffPost.
items.why: It is true and was in the news, but no foreign money, lobbying or paid travel is shown, so it has no clear bearing on criterion 2.

for_review: I used all 4 searches and could not open the Hill article or the Business Insider/Yahoo STOCK Act article. A search snippet of the Yahoo/Insider piece (Aug 2022) says Mast's office called the late Ideal Power disclosure an administrative error with no fine yet. A Pelosi-tracker snippet says an Oct 2022 amendment listed 18 trades filed late, including Aphria/Tilray. I didn't read either page, so check them. Check whether a fine was ever imposed. For item 1, my verdict rests on a read page that says Mast 'may have' missed the deadline, and on that unread corroboration. If you want certainty, open the Insider article. Item 3 (2020 Facebook apology) was not read at all. Item 5: I never read anything on the 2015 Sar-El volunteering, including whether Mast paid his own way. For item 2, a HuffPost search snippet says Mast's office called the Code Pink video 'doctored' and gave a clip with the line 'a 2-year-old Palestinian has to be without sin'. That text was not on the page I opened, so I left it out. The House censure resolution against him (H.Res.846, Nov 2023) was only seen in a search result. For item 4, I didn't read the FTC complaint or the court judgment. A search snippet from IAM says board members were paid, but Mast says he never was. Whether he knew of the board listing is disputed. The owner-sites search (alexjoneslive.com, stewpeters.com, ryandawson.org, infowars.com) turned up nothing about Mast on those sites. AIPAC and AIEF money was not assessed here.
